rules_a_to_k.how: Hint on mel_site: a melanoma of the arm, leg, trunk, chin or forehead with no tissue named is a melanoma of the skin of that region (ICD-O-3.1 manual, printed p. 17).
Hint on mel_site: a site named with a prefix such as peri- or para- takes the tissue the report names; melanoma indicates its tissue, so C76 is not used for a melanoma of a named region.
Hint on mel_site: a melanoma spanning two skin regions with no stated point of origin takes the overlapping-lesion code (.8).
No lymphoma is reached from this tree.
No leukaemia is reached from this tree.

Exclusion options and their reasons state the behaviour (/0, /1, /2) and that the registry records /3 only; the mel_skin_histology hint tells the clerk to record the behaviour the pathologist states. Spitz melanocytoma takes a stated /1 although ICD-O-3.2 prints no 8770/1.
Melanomas carry no ICD-O grade, and the sixth digit is not built (registrar, 7 October 2026).

Question and hint on mel_site: ICD-O-3.2 prints C44._ beside 8720 (Nevoid melanoma), 8721-8723, 8730, 8740-8745, 8761, 8770 and 8780, C69._ beside 8773 and 8774, C70._ beside Melanoma, meningeal and C70.9 beside 8728. With no site stated the printed site is used; a named site wins once the report shows the tumour is not a deposit. The mel_picker hint applies it to spindle cell melanoma type A and B.
mel_picker hint and search: the search matches word roots in any order (melanoma, naevoid and naevoid melanoma find the same entry).
Hint on mel_skin_histology: two melanoma types named for one tumour record the higher code number (amelanotic Spitz melanoma is 8770/3; acral nodular melanoma is 8744/3).

conflicts.issue: The clerk meets primary meningeal melanocytic tumours in the central nervous system. Group III (meningeal lesion triage, group_03_dt.json) already refers every melanin-pigmented or melanocytic meningeal proliferation to Group XI, including meningeal melanocytoma and melanocytosis. XId takes 8720/3 and 8728/3; no ICCC-2017 range takes 8728/0 or 8728/1, so mel_cns excludes them. Group III must keep the referral and add no 8720 or 8728 code.
A tissue-free melanoma at a central nervous system site records 8000/3, which ICCC-2017 places in IIIf, not Group XI.
A melanoma recorded from imaging, or from a clinical note at a non-skin site, records 8000/3, which ICCC-2017 places in XIIb at these sites. The case leaves Group XI.

Group III's secondary-deposit screen sends a deposit whose primary is not known to Group XII. A melanoma deposit with no primary found records 8720/3 at C80.9, which ICCC-2017 places in XId (topography 000-809). The other groups' deposit screens (III, VII, VIII, IX) need a melanoma exception: melanoma of unknown primary stays in Group XI.

Clear cell sarcoma carries the ICD-O-3.2 term Malignant melanoma of soft parts and is IXd7. The melanoma tree refers it to Group IX; Group IX's not-a-sarcoma screen already sends melanoma to Group XI.

WHO skin 5th edition files the CRTC1::TRIM11 cutaneous tumour among soft tissue tumours of the skin, and Sargen 2026 leaves open whether CRTC1::TRIM11 and MED15::ATF1 tumours are melanoma or clear cell sarcoma variants. No code is printed: registrar.
Malignant melanotic nerve sheath tumour (ICD-O-3.2 Related term Melanotic MPNST, 9540/3) is IXb2 and is coded from the Group IX tree; it is not a melanoma code.
Melanotic medulloblastoma is an ICD-O-3.2 Related term of 9470/3 (IIIc1); melanin in an embryonal tumour does not make it a melanoma.

Melanotic neuroectodermal tumour of infancy is listed in the paediatric classification (Pfister 2022, PDF p. 14). ICD-O-3.2 holds 9363/0 only, and ICCC-2017 XIIa6 lists 9363 at /3. It is not a melanoma and is not coded from this tree.

data_gaps.need: An immunohistochemistry panel that decides between melanoma codes
data_gaps.why: No kept source gives one. Melanocytic markers do not separate melanoma from its mimics: the CRTC1::TRIM11 tumour stains for SOX10, S100, melan-A and HMB45 (Goldman-Levy 2025 PDF p. 11), and RNA sequencing separates CRTC1::TRIM11 and MED15::ATF1 tumours from Spitz tumours (Sargen 2026 PDF p. 3). The tree builds no immunohistochemistry checklist; the subtype is the one the histology report names.
